holidays.name: Respect Your Cat Day
holidays.description: A day to give your feline overlord the deference it believes it deserves. Offer treats, honor nap spots, and don't pick up the cat when it clearly doesn't want to be picked up.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrated by cat lovers who suspect the cats were running things all along.
holidays.funFact: Cats sleep roughly 12 to 16 hours a day, so respecting your cat often means tiptoeing around a very busy nap schedule.

holidays.name: National Something on a Stick Day
holidays.description: A celebration of food that comes with its own handle. Corn dogs, kebabs, candy apples, frozen bananas and fair-food experiments all count, and no plate is needed.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It pays tribute to the fairground tradition of putting nearly anything on a stick.
holidays.funFact: Fairs and carnivals have been testing the limits of stick-based cuisine for years. The stick makes food easy to hold in one hand while the other hand carries a lemonade.

holidays.name: Weed Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day to take a second look at the humble weed. Dandelions, clover and other uninvited garden guests get a moment in the sun. Some of them are edible, and many feed pollinators.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It invites gardeners to rethink what counts as a weed.
holidays.funFact: Dandelion leaves, flowers and roots are all edible. The plant's name comes from the French 'dent de lion,' meaning lion's tooth.
